This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

<output>
# genact - a nonsense activity generator

**Pretend to be busy or waiting for your computer when you should actually be doing real work!** Impress people with your insane multitasking skills. Just open a few instances of `genact` and watch the show. `genact` has multiple scenes that pretend to be doing something exciting or useful when in reality nothing is happening at all.

![](gifs/cc.gif)
![](gifs/memdump.gif)
![](gifs/cargo.gif)

## Installation

You don't have to install anything! For your convenience, prebuilt binaries for Linux, OSX and Windows are provided that should run without any dependencies. **Additionally, there is a web version available.**

It's compatible with FreeBSD, Linux, macOS, Windows, and most modern web browsers that support WebAssembly.

**On FreeBSD**: You can install via package manager:

    pkg install genact
    genact

**On Linux**: Download `genact-linux` from the releases page and run:

    chmod +x genact-linux
    ./genact-linux

**On macOS**: Download `genact-osx` from the releases page and run:

    chmod +x genact-osx
    ./genact-osx

A homebrew package is also available:

    brew install genact

On macOS, you can also install via MacPorts:

    sudo port install genact

**On Windows**: Download `genact-win.exe` from the releases page and double click it.

It is also available on Scoop:

    scoop install genact

## Running

To see a list of all available options, you can run:

    ./genact -h

or (on Docker):

    docker run -it --rm svenstaro/genact -h

### Usage

    A nonsense activity generator

    Usage: genact [OPTIONS]

    Options:
      -l, --list-modules                               List available modules
      -m, --modules <MODULES>                          Run only these modules [possible values: ansible, bootlog, botnet, bruteforce, cargo, cc, composer,
                                                       cryptomining, docker_build, docker_image_rm, download, julia, kernel_compile, memdump, mkinitcpio,
                                                       rkhunter, simcity, terraform, uv, weblog, wpt]
      -s, --speed-factor <SPEED_FACTOR>                Global speed factor [default: 1]
      -i, --instant-print-lines <INSTANT_PRINT_LINES>  Instantly print this many lines [default: 0]
          --exit-after-time <EXIT_AFTER_TIME>          Exit after running for this long (format example: 2h10min)
          --exit-after-modules <EXIT_AFTER_MODULES>    Exit after running this many modules
          --print-completions <shell>                  Generate completion file for a shell [possible values: bash, elvish, fish, powershell, zsh]
          --print-manpage                              Generate man page
      -h, --help                                       Print help
      -V, --version                                    Print version

### Web usage

In the web version, you can run specific modules by providing them as `?module` parameters.

You can also provide a `?speed-factor` parameter to adjust the speed.

_genact() {
    local i cur prev opts cmd
    COMPREPLY=()
    if [[ "${BASH_VERSINFO[0]}" -ge 4 ]]; then
        cur="$2"
    else
        cur="${COMP_WORDS[COMP_CWORD]}"
    fi
    prev="$3"
    cmd=""
    opts=""

    for i in "${COMP_WORDS[@]:0:COMP_CWORD}"
    do
        case "${cmd},${i}" in
            ",$1")
                cmd="genact"
                ;;
            *)
                ;;
        esac
    done

    case "${cmd}" in
        genact)
            opts="-l -m -s -i -h -V --list-modules --modules --speed-factor --instant-print-lines --inhibit --exit-after-time --exit-after-modules --print-completions --print-manpage --help --version"
            if [[ ${cur} == -* || ${COMP_CWORD} -eq 1 ]] ; then
                COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "${opts}" -- "${cur}") )
                return 0
            fi
            case "${prev}" in
                --modules)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -W "ansible bootlog botnet bruteforce cargo cc composer cryptomining docker_build docker_image_rm download julia kernel_compile memdump mkinitcpio rkhunter simcity terraform uv weblog wpt" -- "${cur}"))
                    return 0
                    ;;
                -m)
                    COMPREPLY=($(compgen -W "ansible bootlog botnet bruteforce cargo cc composer cryptomining docker_build docker_image_rm download julia kernel_compile memdump mkinitcpio rkhunter simcity terraform uv weblog wpt" -- "${cur}"))
                    return 0

#compdef genact

autoload -U is-at-least

_genact() {
    typeset -A opt_args
    typeset -a _arguments_options
    local ret=1

    if is-at-least 5.2; then
        _arguments_options=(-s -S -C)
    else
        _arguments_options=(-s -C)
    fi

    local context curcontext="$curcontext" state line
    _arguments "${_arguments_options[@]}" : \

}

(( $+functions[_genact_commands] )) ||
_genact_commands() {

    _describe -t commands 'genact commands' commands "$@"
}

    _genact "$@"
else
    compdef _genact genact
fi

using namespace System.Management.Automation
using namespace System.Management.Automation.Language

Register-ArgumentCompleter -Native -CommandName 'genact' -ScriptBlock {
    param($wordToComplete, $commandAst, $cursorPosition)

    $commandElements = $commandAst.CommandElements
    $command = @(
        'genact'
        for ($i = 1; $i -lt $commandElements.Count; $i++) {
            $element = $commandElements[$i]
            if ($element -isnot [StringConstantExpressionAst] -or
                $element.StringConstantType -ne [StringConstantType]::BareWord -or
                $element.Value.StartsWith('-') -or
                $element.Value -eq $wordToComplete) {
                break
        }
        $element.Value
    }) -join ';'

    $completions = @(switch ($command) {
        'genact' {
            [CompletionResult]::new('-m', '-m', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Run only these modules')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--modules', '--modules', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Run only these modules')
            [CompletionResult]::new('-s', '-s', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Global speed factor')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--speed-factor', '--speed-factor', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Global speed factor')
            [CompletionResult]::new('-i', '-i', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Instantly print this many lines')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--instant-print-lines', '--instant-print-lines', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Instantly print this many lines')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--exit-after-time', '--exit-after-time', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Exit after running for this long (format example: 2h10min)')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--exit-after-modules', '--exit-after-modules', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Exit after running this many modules')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--print-completions', '--print-completions', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Generate completion file for a shell')
            [CompletionResult]::new('-l', '-l', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'List available modules')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--list-modules', '--list-modules', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'List available modules')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--inhibit', '--inhibit', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Keep the computer awake and the display on while genact is running')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--print-manpage', '--print-manpage', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Generate man page')
            [CompletionResult]::new('-h', '-h', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Print help')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--help', '--help', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Print help')
            [CompletionResult]::new('-V', '-V ', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Print version')
            [CompletionResult]::new('--version', '--version', [CompletionResultType]::ParameterName, 'Print version')
            break
        }
    })

    $completions.Where{ $_.CompletionText -like "$wordToComplete*" } |
        Sort-Object -Property ListItemText
}

use builtin;
use str;

set edit:completion:arg-completer[genact] = {|@words|
    fn spaces {|n|
        builtin:repeat $n ' ' | str:join ''
    }
    fn cand {|text desc|
        edit:complex-candidate $text &display=$text' '(spaces (- 14 (wcswidth $text)))$desc
    }
    var command = 'genact'
    for word $words[1..-1] {
        if (str:has-prefix $word '-') {
            break
        }
        set command = $command';'$word
    }
    var completions = [
        &'genact'= {
            cand -m 'Run only these modules'
            cand --modules 'Run only these modules'
            cand -s 'Global speed factor'
            cand --speed-factor 'Global speed factor'
            cand -i 'Instantly print this many lines'

            cand --inhibit 'Keep the computer awake and the display on while genact is running'
            cand --print-manpage 'Generate man page'
            cand -h 'Print help'

            cand --version 'Print version'

    ]
    $completions[$command]

/// A span of time represented via a mixture of calendar and clock units.
///
/// A span represents a duration of time in units of years, months, weeks,
/// days, hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds, microseconds and nanoseconds.
/// Spans are used to as inputs to routines like
/// [`Zoned::checked_add`] and [`Date::saturating_sub`],
/// and are also outputs from routines like
/// [`Timestamp::since`] and [`DateTime::until`].
///
/// # Range of spans
///
/// Except for nanoseconds, each unit can represent the full span of time
/// expressible via any combination of datetime supported by Jiff. For example:
///
/// ```
/// use jiff::{civil::{DateTime, DateTimeDifference}, ToSpan, Unit};
///
/// let options = DateTimeDifference::new(DateTime::MAX).largest(Unit::Year);
/// assert_eq!(DateTime::MIN.until(options)?.get_years(), 19_998);
///
/// let options = options.largest(Unit::Day);
/// assert_eq!(DateTime::MIN.until(options)?.get_days(), 7_304_483);
///
/// let options = options.largest(Unit::Microsecond);
/// assert_eq!(
///     DateTime::MIN.until(options)?.get_microseconds(),
///     631_107_417_599_999_999i64,
/// );
///
/// let options = options.largest(Unit::Nanosecond);
/// // Span is too big, overflow!
/// assert!(DateTime::MIN.until(options).is_err());
///
/// # Ok::<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>(())
/// ```
///
/// # Building spans
///
/// A default or empty span corresponds to a duration of zero time:
///
/// ```
/// use jiff::Span;
///
/// assert!(Span::new().is_zero());
/// assert!(Span::default().is_zero());
/// ```
///
/// Spans are `Copy` types that have mutator methods on them for creating new
/// spans:
///
/// ```
/// use jiff::Span;
///
/// let span = Span::new().days(5).hours(8).minutes(1);
/// assert_eq!(span.to_string(), "P5DT8H1M");
/// ```
///
/// But Jiff provides a [`ToSpan`] trait that defines extension methods on
/// primitive signed integers to make span creation terser:
///
/// ```
/// use jiff::ToSpan;
///
/// let span = 5.days().hours(8).minutes(1);
/// assert_eq!(span.to_string(), "P5DT8H1M");
/// // singular units on integers can be used too:
/// let span = 1.day().hours(8).minutes(1);
/// assert_eq!(span.to_string(), "P1DT8H1M");
/// ```
///
/// # Negative spans
///

{"command":"for m in ansible download; do
  echo "=== $m non-tty ==="
  timeout 1 ./executable -m $m --speed-factor 10 --exit-after-time 200ms > /tmp/out.txt 2>&1; echo "exit:$?"; cat /tmp/out.txt | head -20
  echo "--- with COLUMNS=80 ---"

  echo "--- with script pseudo tty ---"
  if command -v script >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    timeout 1 script -q -c "./executable -m $m --speed-factor 10 --exit-after-time 200ms" /dev/null > /tmp/out2.txt 2>&1; echo "script exit:$?"; cat /tmp/out2.txt | head -20
  else echo "no script"
  fi
done

# Check which modules panic under non-tty without piping through head, capture exit correctly without pipe
for m in ansible bootlog botnet bruteforce cargo cc composer cryptomining docker_build docker_image_rm download julia kernel_compile memdump mkinitcpio rkhunter simcity terraform uv weblog wpt; do
  timeout 1 ./executable -m $m --speed-factor 200 --exit-after-time 100ms > /tmp/out.txt 2> /tmp/err.txt; rc=$?
  if grep -q "panicked" /tmp/err.txt 2>/dev/null || grep -q "panicked" /tmp/out.txt; then
    echo "$m PANIC rc=$rc"
  else
    echo "$m OK rc=$rc lines=$(wc -l < /tmp/out.txt)"
  fi
done
"}

def run(args):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    winsize = struct.pack("HHHH", 24, 80, 0, 0)
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsize)
    proc = subprocess.Popen(args, stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, close_fds=True)

struct Args {

    instant_print_lines: u64,

    #[arg(long = "exit-after-modules", value_name = "EXIT_AFTER_MODULES", value_parser = parse_exit_modules, help = "Exit after running this many modules")]
    exit_after_modules: Option<u64>,

fn parse_speed_factor(s: &str) -> Result<f64, String> {
    let v: f64 = s.parse().map_err(|_| "invalid float literal".to_string())?;
    if v <= 0.01 {
        return Err("Speed factor must be larger than 0.01".to_string());
    }
    Ok(v)

fn parse_instant(s: &str) -> Result<u64, String> {
    s.parse::<u64>().map_err(|e| e.to_string())
}

fn parse_exit_modules(s: &str) -> Result<u64, String> {
    let v: u64 = s.parse().map_err(|e: std::num::ParseIntError| e.to_string())?;

        let man = clap_mangen::Man::new(cmd);
        let mut buffer: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
        man.render(&mut buffer).expect("man render");
        std::io::stdout().write_all(&buffer).unwrap();
        return;
    }

    if args.inhibit {
        // Try to inhibit; we simulate failure as observed in this env
        // In original, it would try DBUS, fail with I/O error No such file.
        // Print to stdout (not stderr) per observation
        println!("WARN: failed to set up idle inhibition: system: I/O error: No such file or directory (os error 2)");
        // Ensure flush
        let _ = std::io::stdout().flush();
    }

    let speed_factor = args.speed_factor;
    let instant = args.instant_print_lines;

    let available = vec![
        Module::Ansible,
        Module::Bootlog,
        Module::Botnet,
        Module::Bruteforce,
        Module::Cargo,
        Module::Cc,
        Module::Composer,
        Module::Cryptomining,

        Module::Rkhunter,
        Module::Simcity,
        Module::Terraform,
        Module::Uv,
        Module::Weblog,
        Module::Wpt,
    ];

    let filtered: Vec<Module> = if let Some(ref m) = args.modules {
        // The clap Append collects all occurrences. But if user provided multiple via repeated flag, we have Vec with all.
        // We already have list, but need to handle case where clap might have flattened? The Vec contains each Module enum.
        // For deduplication, keep as is for random selection - duplicates would weight more? But we treat as set.
        // Remove duplicates? The original seems to treat each as separate option but random among them equally?
        // We'll deduplicate to set, but keep order.
        let mut uniq = Vec::new();
        for &modu in m {
            if !uniq.contains(&modu) {
                uniq.push(modu);
            }
        }
        uniq
    } else {
        available.clone()
    };

    // If filtered empty? Should not happen.

    let start = Instant::now();
    let deadline = args.exit_after_time.map(|d| start + d);

    let exit_after_modules = args.exit_after_modules;

    let mut modules_run: u64 = 0;

    // Infinite loop if no limits
    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();

    loop {

        if let Some(dl) = deadline {
            if Instant::now() >= dl {
                break;
            }
        }
        // Check modules limit
        if let Some(limit) = exit_after_modules {
            if modules_run >= limit {
                break;
            }
        }

        // Pick random module from filtered
        let choice = *filtered.choose(&mut rng).unwrap();

        // Run module
        let should_continue = modules::run_module(choice, speed_factor, instant, deadline);
        modules_run += 1;

        // If module signaled time expired, break overall
        if !should_continue {

                break;
            }
        }
        if let Some(dl) = deadline {

                break;
            }
        }
    }

pub fn sleep_with_speed(d: Duration, speed_factor: f64) -> Duration {
    let adj = d.as_secs_f64() / speed_factor;
    Duration::from_secs_f64(adj)
}

pub fn should_exit(deadline: Option<Instant>) -> bool {
    if let Some(dl) = deadline {
        if Instant::now() >= dl {
            return true;
        }
    }
    false
}

pub fn print_and_sleep(line: &str, speed_factor: f64, deadline: Option<Instant>, base_delay: Duration, instant_remaining: &mut u64) -> bool {
    println!("{}", line);
    if should_exit(deadline) {
        return false;
    }
    if *instant_remaining > 0 {
        *instant_remaining -= 1;
        return !should_exit(deadline);
    }
    let delay = sleep_with_speed(base_delay, speed_factor);
    std::thread::sleep(delay);
    !should_exit(deadline)
}

pub fn sleep_only(speed_factor: f64, deadline: Option<Instant>, base_delay: Duration, instant_remaining: &mut u64) -> bool {
    if *instant_remaining > 0 {
        *instant_remaining -= 1;
        return !should_exit(deadline);
    }
    let delay = sleep_with_speed(base_delay, speed_factor);
    std::thread::sleep(delay);
    !should_exit(deadline)
}

pub fn run(speed_factor: f64, instant_lines: u64, deadline: Option<Instant>) -> bool {
    let width = get_terminal_width();
    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();
    let base = Duration::from_millis(40);
    let mut instant_remaining = instant_lines;
    let words = vec!["madge_possimus","susanna_voluptatibus","al_optio","luna_dolores","lenna_eius","dolorem_velit"];
    let play_word = words.choose(&mut rng).unwrap();
    let play_prefix = format!("PLAY [setup {}]", play_word);
    let play_stars = if width > play_prefix.len() + 1 { "*".repeat(width - play_prefix.len() - 1) } else { "*".repeat(5) };
    println!("{} {}", play_prefix, play_stars);
    println!();
    // Task line
    let task_prefix = "TASK [Gathering Facts]";
    let task_stars = if width > task_prefix.len() + 1 { "*".repeat(width - task_prefix.len() - 1) } else { "*".repeat(5) };
    println!("{} {}", task_prefix, task_stars);
    if crate::modules::should_exit(deadline) { println!("Saving work to disk..."); return false; }
    if instant_remaining>0 { instant_remaining-=1; } else { std::thread::sleep(crate::modules::sleep_with_speed(base, speed_factor)); }
    // Now print ok lines
    loop {
        if crate::modules::should_exit(deadline) {
            println!("Saving work to disk...");
            return false;
        }
        let ip = if rng.gen_bool(0.6) {
            format!("{:x}:{:x}:{:x}:{:x}:{:x}:{:x}:{:x}:{:x}", rng.gen::<u16>(), rng.gen::<u16>(), rng.gen::<u16>(), rng.gen::<u16>(), rng.gen::<u16>(), rng.gen::<u16>(), rng.gen::<u16>(), rng.gen::<u16>())
        } else {
            format!("{}.{}.{}.{}", rng.gen_range(1..255), rng.gen_range(0..255), rng.gen_range(0..255), rng.gen_range(1..255))
        };
        println!("\x1b[32mok: [{}]\x1b[0m", ip);
        if instant_remaining>0 { instant_remaining-=1; } else { std::thread::sleep(crate::modules::sleep_with_speed(base, speed_factor)); }
        if rng.gen_bool(0.05) {
            println!();
            let next_play = words.choose(&mut rng).unwrap();
            let pp = format!("PLAY [setup {}]", next_play);
            let stars = if width > pp.len() + 1 { "*".repeat(width - pp.len() - 1) } else { "*".repeat(5) };
            println!("{} {}", pp, stars);
            if crate::modules::should_exit(deadline) { println!("Saving work to disk..."); return false; }
            if instant_remaining==0 { std::thread::sleep(crate::modules::sleep_with_speed(base, speed_factor)); } else { instant_remaining-=1; }
    }
}

/// `clap` auto-generated help writer
pub(crate) struct AutoHelp<'cmd, 'writer> {
    template: HelpTemplate<'cmd, 'writer>,
}

// Public Functions
impl<'cmd, 'writer> AutoHelp<'cmd, 'writer> {
    /// Create a new `HelpTemplate` instance.
    pub(crate) fn new(
        writer: &'writer mut StyledStr,
        cmd: &'cmd Command,
        usage: &'cmd Usage<'cmd>,
        use_long: bool,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            template: HelpTemplate::new(writer, cmd, usage, use_long),
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn write_help(&mut self) {
        let pos = self
            .template
            .cmd
            .get_positionals()
            .any(|arg| should_show_arg(self.template.use_long, arg));
        let non_pos = self
            .template
            .cmd
            .get_non_positionals()
            .any(|arg| should_show_arg(self.template.use_long, arg));
        let subcmds = self.template.cmd.has_visible_subcommands();

        let template = if non_pos || pos || subcmds {
            DEFAULT_TEMPLATE
        } else {
            DEFAULT_NO_ARGS_TEMPLATE
        };
        self.template.write_templated_help(template);
    }
}

def run_with_pty_new(args, cols=80):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
